text: In eighteen sixty-seven, Russia sold a piece of land bigger than Germany, France and Spain combined.
The price? About two cents an acre.
The buyer was America. The land was Alaska. And not long after, people found gold there. Then oil.
[checking his pocket watch, wincing] Oof. Worst garage sale in history.
But here's the weird part. Russia barely missed it. Because even without Alaska, Russia is still the biggest country on Earth.
It covers eleven time zones. When Moscow is brushing its teeth before bed, the far east of Russia is already eating tomorrow's breakfast.

And over eleven hundred years, this land has been run by Viking chiefs, Mongol khans, a tsar who killed his own son, a giant who shaved his nobles' beards by force, a German princess who took her husband's throne, and a dictator who erased people from photos.
[nervous] I've been to their family dinners. Bring a helmet.
But look closely, and Russia keeps living the same story.
First, chaos. Then one man grabs total control. People trade their freedom for order. Then that control goes too far, everything collapses... and the story starts again.
Vikings. Mongols. Tsars. Communists. Different hats. Same story.
So how did a bunch of feuding forest tribes build the largest country in history? And why can't Russia escape that cycle?
[winding his watch] Hold on to something.
Let's go back to the very beginning.
About twelve hundred years ago, there was no Russia. Just forest, swamp... and rivers. So many rivers.
Along them lived tribes called the East Slavs. They farmed, they hunted, they traded fur. And they had one big problem.
They could not. Stop. Fighting.
So, the story goes, they did something no one expected. They asked foreigners to come and rule them.
And not just any foreigners. Vikings.
[dictating] "Dear Vikings. Our land is huge and rich... but nobody is in charge."
[horrified] The Vikings? The ones who raid monasteries for fun?
You have a better plan?
We could... stop fighting each other?
[laughing] Hah! Good one.
Sign it.
[to camera] Historians aren't sure that letter ever happened. But it's a great story.
According to Russia's oldest history book, in eight sixty-two, a Viking named Rurik arrived and took charge of the trading town of Novgorod.
The locals called these Vikings the Rus. And that is where the name Russia comes from.
Rurik's family would rule this land for more than seven hundred years.
After Rurik, a Viking named Oleg sailed south down the river and grabbed a rich town on the Dnieper: Kyiv.
Kyiv sat on the trade road between the Baltic Sea and the richest city on Earth, Constantinople. Furs and honey went south. Silver and silk came north.
Their new state is called Kievan Rus. Chaos had produced... one ruling family. Order.
[making a note] Loop step one. Check.
Then came a ruler with the scariest revenge story in Russian history: Princess Olga.
In nine forty-five, a tribe called the Drevlians killed her husband, Prince Igor, for demanding too much tax.
Then they sent men to propose that Olga marry their prince.
Great Princess! Our prince would like to marry you!
[sweetly] How lovely. Come. I'll give you a great welcome.
The story goes she had the first group buried alive, still in their boat. The second group was invited to a nice warm bathhouse... and the doors were locked.
[hiding behind his watch] Never accept a spa invitation in the tenth century.
And then, legend says, she burned the Drevlians' capital to the ground.
Strangely, the church later made her a saint.
A saint? Bold choice.
Her grandson Vladimir made the decision that still shapes Russia today: its religion.
The story goes he interviewed religions like job candidates.
[shivering] No alcohol? In this winter? [shakes head] Next.
[whispering] Sire... the churches in Constantinople are beautiful.
Now we're talking.
In about nine eighty-eight, Vladimir chose Orthodox Christianity, and had the people of Kyiv baptized in the river.
Kievan Rus was now rich, Christian and connected to the greatest city in the world. Under his son Yaroslav the Wise, it was one of the biggest states in Europe.
And then... the family did what this family always did.
[sighing] They started fighting each other.
Brothers fought brothers. Cousins fought cousins. The state split into a dozen squabbling princedoms.
Chaos, again.
And while the princes were busy fighting each other... far to the east, the most terrifying army in human history had just started riding west.
[watch alarm ringing, eyes wide] Oh no. It's them.
